translations.text: The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave him to show his servants what must happen soon. He made it known by sending his angel to his servant John,
who testified to the word of God and to the testimony of Jesus Christ—to everything he saw.
Blessed is the one who reads, and those who hear the words of this prophecy and keep what is written in it, for the time is near.
John, to the seven churches in Asia: Grace and peace to you from the one who is, who was, and who is coming, and from the seven spirits before his throne,
and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth. To him who loves us and frees us from our sins by his blood,
and has made us a priestly kingdom for his God and Father—to him be glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.
Look, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, even those who pierced him. All the tribes of the earth will mourn over him. Yes, amen.
“I am Alaph and Taw,” says the Lord God, who is, who was, and who is coming, the Almighty.
I, John, your brother and your partner in the suffering and endurance that are in Jesus, was on the island called Patmos because of the word of God and because of the testimony of Jesus Christ.
I was in the Spirit on Sunday, and I heard behind me a loud voice like a trumpet,
saying, “Write what you see in a book and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.”
I turned to find out whose voice was speaking to me. When I turned, I saw seven golden lampstands,
and among the lampstands someone resembling a human being, wearing an ephod, with a golden sash tied around his chest.
His head and his hair were white like wool and like snow, and his eyes were like a flame of fire.
His feet were like Lebanese bronze heated in a furnace, and his voice was like the sound of many waters.
He had seven stars in his right hand, and a sharp spear came out of his mouth. His appearance was like the sun shining in its strength.
When I saw him, I fell at his feet as though dead. He laid his right hand on me, saying, “Do not be afraid. I am the first and the last,
and the living one. I was dead, and look, I am alive forever and ever. Amen. I have the key of death and of Sheol.
So write what you have seen, what is, and what is going to happen after these things.

As for the mystery of the seven stars you saw in my right hand and the seven lampstands: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven golden lampstands you saw are the seven churches.”
“Write to the angel in the church of Ephesus: This is what the one who holds the seven stars in his hand says, the one who walks among the golden lampstands:
I know your deeds, your hard work, and your endurance, and that you cannot tolerate evil people. You have tested those who call themselves apostles but are not, and you have found them to be liars.
You have endurance, and you have borne hardships for my name and have not grown weary.
But I have this against you: you have abandoned your first love.
Remember where you departed from, and do the deeds you did at first. Otherwise, I am coming against you and will remove your lampstand, unless you repent.
But you have this in your favor: you hate the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
Let anyone who has ears hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who overcomes, I will give food from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God.
Write to the angel of the church in Smyrna: This is what the First and the Last says, the one who was dead and came to life.
I know your suffering and your poverty—yet you are rich—and the blasphemy of those who call themselves Jews but are not Jews. Instead, they are a synagogue of Satan.

Do not be afraid of anything you are about to suffer. Look, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison so that you may be tested, and you will suffer for ten days. Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.
Let anyone who has ears hear what the Spirit says to the churches. The one who overcomes will not be harmed by the second death.
Write to the angel in the church in Pergamum: This is what the one who has the sharp, two-edged sword says.

I know where you live, where Satan’s throne is. You hold firmly to my name and have not denied faith in me. And in those days you contended, and my faithful witness [?], because every witness of mine is faithful—the one who was killed among you.

But I have a few things against you: you have people there who hold to the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to put a stumbling block before the people of Israel, so that they would eat food sacrificed to idols and commit sexual immorality.
Likewise, you also have people who hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans in the same way.
Repent, then. Otherwise, I am coming against you soon, and I will fight against them with the sword of my mouth.

Let anyone who has ears hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who overcomes, I will give some of the hidden manna. I will also give that person a white stone, and on the stone a new name is written, which no one knows except the one who receives it.
Write to the angel in the church in Thyatira: This is what the Son of God says, whose eye is like a flame of fire and whose feet are like Lebanese bronze.
I know your deeds, your love, your faith, your service, and your endurance. Your later deeds are more numerous than your earlier ones.
But I have much against you: you tolerate your wife Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess and teaches and leads my servants astray to commit sexual immorality and eat food sacrificed to idols.
I gave her time to repent, but she is unwilling to repent of her sexual immorality.
Look, I am throwing her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her into great suffering, unless they repent of their deeds.
I will put her children to death, and all the churches will know that I am the one who searches the innermost feelings and the heart. I will give each of you according to your deeds.
I say to you, the rest in Thyatira, all who do not hold this teaching, who have not known the deep things of Satan, as they say: I will place no other burden on you.
But hold firmly to what you have until I come.
To the one who overcomes and keeps my works, I will give authority over the nations,
to shepherd them with an iron rod; and you will crush them like a potter’s vessels. For this is what I too received from my Father.
And I will give him the morning star.
Whoever has ears should hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

And to the angel in the church of Sardis write: This is what the one who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars says: I know your works and the reputation you have, that you are alive, yet you are dead.
Be watchful, and strengthen those who remain, who were about to die [?]. For I have not found your works complete before God.
Remember how you heard and received. Be attentive and repent. But if you do not wake up, I will come upon you like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come upon you.
But I have a few names in Sardis, those who have not stained their clothes. They walk before me in white, and they are worthy.
The one who overcomes will likewise be clothed in white garments. I will not erase his name from the book of life, and I will acknowledge his name before my Father and before his angels.
Anyone who has ears should hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
And to the angel of the church of Philadelphia write: This is what the Holy and True One says, the one who has the keys of David, who opens and no one shuts, and shuts and no one opens:
I know your works. Look, I have placed before you an open door that no one can shut, because you have little strength, yet you have kept my word and have not denied my name.

Look, I am giving you some from the synagogue of Satan, from those who say that they are Jews but are not, and are lying. Look, I will make them come and bow down before your feet, and they will know that I have loved you.
Because you have kept my word about endurance, I too will keep you from the trial that is about to come upon the whole inhabited world to test those who live on the earth.
I am coming soon. Hold firmly to what you have, so that no one takes your crown.

The one who overcomes I will make a pillar in the temple of God, and he will never go outside again. I will write on him the name of my God and the name of the new city, Jerusalem, which comes down from my God, and my own new name.
Whoever has ears should hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
And to the angel of the church of Laodicea write: This is what the Amen says, the faithful and true witness, and the beginning of God’s creation:
I know your works. You are neither cold nor hot. You ought to be either cold or hot.
You are lukewarm, neither cold nor hot. I am about to vomit you out of my mouth.
Because you have said that you are rich, “I have become wealthy and need nothing,” yet you do not know that you are weak and miserable, poor and naked.

I advise you to buy from me gold refined by fire so that you may become rich, and white clothes to wear so that the shame of your nakedness will not be exposed. And apply eye salve so that you may see.
I rebuke and discipline those whom I love. So be zealous and repent.
Look, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with him, and he with me.
To the one who overcomes, I will grant a seat with me on my throne, just as I overcame and sat down with my Father on his throne.
Let anyone who has ears hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

After these things I looked, and there was an open door in heaven. And the voice I had heard, like a trumpet, spoke with me, saying, “Come up here, and I will show you what is appointed to happen after these things.”
Immediately I was in the Spirit. And there was a throne set in heaven, with someone sitting on the throne.
The one sitting there had the appearance of jasper and carnelian stone. A rainbow around the throne had the appearance of emeralds.
Around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and on the thrones sat twenty-four elders, dressed in white clothes, with gold crowns on their heads.
From the thrones came thunder, lightning, and voices. Seven lamps burned before the throne; these are the seven spirits of God.
Before the throne was a sea of glass resembling ice. In the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures, full of eyes in front and behind.
The first living creature was like a lion. The second living creature resembled a calf. The third living creature had a face like a human being's. The fourth living creature resembled a flying eagle.

Each of the four living creatures stood with six wings all around it, from its claws upward. Inside they were full of eyes. Day and night they never stop saying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is coming.”
Whenever the four living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to the one sitting on the throne, to the one who lives forever and ever, amen,
the twenty-four elders will fall down before the one sitting on the throne and worship the one who lives forever and ever, amen. They will cast their crowns before the throne, saying,
“You are worthy, our Lord and our God, to receive glory, honor, and power, because you created everything, and by your will all things existed and were created.”
I saw in the right hand of the one sitting on the throne a scroll with writing on the inside and outside, sealed with seven seals.
I saw another mighty angel proclaiming in a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?”
No one in heaven or on earth or beneath the earth was able to open the scroll, break its seals, or look at it.
I wept bitterly because no one was found worthy to open the scroll and break its seals.
And one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep. Look, the Lion from the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has conquered. He will open the scroll and its seals.”

And I saw, in the midst of the throne and the four living creatures and the elders, a Lamb standing as though it had been slaughtered. It had seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth.
And he came and took the scroll from the hand of the one seated on the throne.

And when he took the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb. Each of them had a harp and a golden bowl full of incense, which is the prayers of the holy ones.

They sing a new song of praise, saying, “You are worthy to take the scroll and to open its seals, because you were slaughtered and with your blood purchased us for God from every tribe and people and nation.
And you made them a kingdom and priests and kings for our God, and they will reign on the earth.”

And I looked and heard what sounded like the voice of many angels around the throne and the living creatures and the elders. Their number was ten thousand times ten thousand and a thousand times a thousand.
They were saying in a loud voice, “You are worthy, slaughtered Lamb, to receive power and wealth and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing.”

And I heard every creature in heaven and on earth and beneath the earth and in the sea, and everything in them, saying, “To the one seated on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing and honor and glory and dominion forever and ever.”
And the four living creatures were saying, “Amen.” And the elders fell down and worshiped.
And I watched as the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying in a voice like thunder, “Come and see.”
I heard and saw, and there was a white horse. Its rider had a bow, and a crown was given to him. He went out victorious, conquering, and to conquer.
And when he opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, “Come.”
And a red horse came out. Its rider was given permission to take peace from the earth, so that people would slaughter one another. And he was given a great sword.
And when the third seal was opened, I heard the third living creature saying, “Come.” And there was a black horse, and its rider had a set of scales in his hand.
And I heard a voice from among the living creatures saying, “A measure of wheat for a denarius, and three measures of barley for a denarius. And do not harm the wine and the oil.”
And when he opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of a living creature saying, “Come.”

And I saw a pale green horse. Its rider’s name was Death, and Sheol followed him. And he was given authority over a quarter of the earth, to kill with the sword and with famine and with death and with the wild beasts of the earth.
And when he opened the fifth seal, I saw beneath the altar the souls of those who had been killed because of the word of God and because of the testimony of Jesus that they held.
And they cried out in a loud voice, saying, “How long, holy and true Lord, will you refrain from judging and avenging our blood on the inhabitants of the earth?”

And each one of them was given a white robe, and they were told to rest a little longer, until their fellow servants and their brothers, who were to be killed as they had been, were also complete in number.
And I saw when he opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake. The sun became black like sackcloth made of hair, and the whole moon became like blood.
And the stars of heaven fell to the earth, like a fig tree dropping its unripe figs when shaken by a strong wind.
And the heavens parted and rolled up like scrolls, and every mountain and every island were moved from their places.
And the kings of the earth, the great men, the commanders of thousands, the rich, the armed forces, and all slaves and free people hid themselves in caves and among the rocks of the mountains.
And they said to the mountains and rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of the Lamb.”
For the great day of their wrath has come, and who can stand?
And after this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding back the four winds so that no wind would blow on the earth or on the sea or on any tree.

And I saw another angel rising from the direction of the sunrise, holding the seal of the living God. He called out in a loud voice to the four angels who had been given permission to harm the earth and the sea.
He said, “Do not harm the earth, the sea, or the trees until we have sealed God’s servants on their foreheads.”
And I heard the number of those who were sealed: one hundred and forty-four thousand, from all the tribes of Israel.
From the tribe of Judah, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Reuben, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Gad, twelve thousand.
From the tribe of Asher, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Naphtali, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Manasseh, twelve thousand.
From the tribe of Simeon, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Issachar, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Levi, twelve thousand.
From the tribe of Zebulun, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Joseph, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Benjamin, twelve thousand sealed.

After this I saw a great crowd that no one could count, from every people and tribe and nation and language, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.
And they cried out in a loud voice, saying, “Salvation belongs to our God, and to the one who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb.”
And all the angels were standing around the throne and the elders and the four living creatures, and they fell on their faces before the throne,
saying, “Amen! Praise and blessing and wisdom and thanksgiving and honor and power and might belong to our God forever and ever. Amen!”
And one of the elders spoke and said to me, “Who are these people wearing white robes, and where did they come from?”
And I said to him, “My lord, you know.” And he said to me, “These are the ones who came out of the great tribulation. They washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.”
For this reason they are before the throne of God and serve him day and night in his temple, and the one who sits on the throne will shelter them.
They will neither hunger nor thirst. The sun will not strike them, nor will any scorching heat.
For the Lamb in the middle of the throne will shepherd them and lead them to life and to springs of water, and he will wipe every tear from their eyes.
When he opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.
I saw the seven angels who stood before God, and they were given seven trumpets.
Another angel came and stood at the altar, holding a golden censer. He was given much incense to offer with the prayers of all the holy ones on the altar before the throne.
The smoke of the incense rose with the prayers of the holy ones from the angel’s hand before God.
The angel took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and threw it onto the earth. There were thunderclaps, voices, lightning, and an earthquake.
The seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound them.

The first sounded his trumpet, and there was hail and fire mixed with water, and they were thrown onto the earth. A third of the earth was burned up, a third of the trees were burned up, and all the grass of the earth was burned up.
The second sounded his trumpet, and something like a great burning mountain fell into the sea. A third of the sea became blood.
A third of all the living creatures in the sea died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
The third sounded his trumpet, and a great star fell from heaven, burning like a flame. It fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water.
The star's name is Wormwood. A third of the waters became like wormwood, and many people died because the waters had become bitter.

The fourth sounded his trumpet, and a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars were struck, so that a third of them became dark. The day gave no light for a third of its duration, and likewise the night.
I heard an eagle flying in heaven say, “Woe, woe, woe to the inhabitants of the earth because of the sound of the trumpets of the three angels who are about to sound them!”
The fifth sounded his trumpet, and I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to the earth. It was given the key to the pits of the abyss.
Smoke rose from the pits like smoke from a great blazing furnace. The sun and the air were darkened by the smoke from the pits.
Locusts came out of the smoke onto the earth, and they were given power like that of the earth's scorpions.
They were told not to harm the grass of the earth, any green plant, or any tree, but only those people who did not have God's seal on their foreheads.
They were allowed not to kill them, but to have them tormented for five months. Their torment was like the torment caused by a scorpion when it attacks a person.
In those days people will seek death but will not find it. They will long to die, but death will flee from them.
The locusts looked like horses prepared for battle. On their heads were what looked like crowns resembling gold, and their faces were like human faces.
They had hair like women's hair, and their teeth were like lions' teeth.
They had armor like iron armor, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots with many horses rushing into battle.
They have tails like those of scorpions, with stings in their tails, and their power is to injure people for five months.
They have a king over them, the angel of the abyss, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and whose name in Aramaic is Shara.
One woe has passed. Look, two more woes are coming.
After these things, the sixth angel sounded, and I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar before God.
It said to the sixth angel, who had the trumpet, “Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates.”
And the four angels were released, those who had been prepared for the hour and the day and the month and the year, to kill a third of humanity.
The number of the cavalry troops was two hundred million; I heard their number.

This is how I saw the horses in the vision: those riding them had breastplates of fire and carbuncle [?] sulfur. The heads of their horses were like lions’ heads, and fire, sulfur, and smoke came out of their mouths.
A third of humanity was killed by these three plagues, and by the fire, sulfur, and smoke coming out of their mouths.
For the power of the horses is in their mouths and also in their tails.

The rest of humanity, who were not killed by these plagues, did not repent of the works of their hands and stop worshiping demons and idols of gold, silver, bronze, wood, and stone, which cannot see or hear or walk.
Nor did they repent of their murders, their sorceries, or their sexual immorality.
I saw another angel coming down from heaven, wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow over his head. His appearance was like the sun, and his feet were like pillars of fire.
He had an open little scroll in his hand. He placed his right foot on the sea and his left on the land.
He cried out with a loud voice, like a lion roaring. When he cried out, seven thunders spoke with their voices.
When the seven thunders spoke, I was about to write. But I heard a voice from heaven [?] saying, “Seal up what the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write it down.”
The angel whom I had seen standing on the sea and on the dry land raised his hand to heaven.
He swore by the one who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and everything in it, and the earth and everything in it, that there would be no more delay.
But in the days of the seventh angel, when he is about to sound, the mystery of God will be fulfilled, as he announced the good news to his servants the prophets.
Again I heard a voice from heaven speaking with me and saying, “Go, take the little scroll in the hand of the angel standing on the land and on the sea.”
I went to the angel and asked him to give me the little scroll. He said to me, “Take it and eat it. It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be like honey.”
I took the little scroll from the angel’s hand and ate it. In my mouth it was sweet as honey, but when I had eaten it, my stomach became bitter.
He said to me, “You are given another opportunity to prophesy about peoples, nations, languages, and many kings.”
I was given a reed like a rod. An angel was standing there and said, “Get up and measure God’s temple and the altar and those who worship in it.”
But leave out the courtyard inside the temple and do not measure it, because it has been given to the nations. They will trample the holy city for forty-two months.
I will grant my two witnesses the ability to prophesy for one thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.
These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the whole earth.
If anyone wants to harm them, fire comes out of their mouths and consumes their enemies. Anyone who wants to harm them is to be killed in this way.

These have authority to shut the sky so that no rain falls during the days of their prophesying. They have authority to turn water into blood and to strike the earth with every kind of plague as often as they wish.
When they have finished their testimony, the beast that comes up from the sea will make war against them, conquer them, and kill them.
Their corpses will lie in the streets of the great city, which is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord was crucified.
People from the nations, tribes, languages, and peoples will look at their corpses for three and a half days, and they will not allow their corpses to be placed in tombs.
The inhabitants of the earth will rejoice over them and celebrate, and they will send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented the inhabitants of the earth.
After three and a half days, a living spirit from God entered them, and they stood on their feet. A spirit of life fell upon them, and great fear came upon those who saw them.
They heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them, “Come up here.” They went up to heaven in a cloud, while their enemies watched them.
At that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell. Seven thousand men were killed in the earthquake. The rest were afraid and gave glory to the God of heaven.
Look, two woes have passed, and look, the third woe is coming immediately.
The seventh angel cried out, and there were loud voices in heaven saying, “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our God and of his Messiah, and he reigns forever and ever.”
The twenty-four elders who sit on their thrones before God fell on their faces and worshiped God,
saying, “We give you thanks, Lord God Almighty, who is and who was, because you have taken up your great power and begun to reign.”

The nations were angry, and your wrath has come, along with the time for the dead to be judged, for you to reward your servants the prophets, the holy ones, and those who fear your name, small and great alike, and to destroy those who have destroyed the earth.
The temple in heaven was opened, and the ark of his covenant was seen in the temple. There were flashes of lightning, thunder, voices, an earthquake, and heavy hail.
A great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon beneath her feet and a crown of twelve stars on her head.
She was pregnant and crying out, suffering labor pains and the agony of giving birth.
Another sign appeared in heaven: look, a great fiery dragon with seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns on its heads.

Its tail swept along a third of the stars in heaven and threw them down to the earth. The dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth it could devour her son.
She gave birth to a son, a male child, who is to shepherd all the nations with an iron rod. Her son was snatched up to God and to his throne.
And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she had a place prepared by God, so that they could feed her there for one thousand two hundred and sixty days.
And war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.
But they could not prevail, and no place was found for them in heaven.
And the great dragon was thrown down—that ancient serpent called the Devil and Satan, who led the whole earth astray. He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him.

And I heard a loud voice from heaven saying, “Look! The salvation, power, and kingdom of our God have come, because the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, the one who accused them night and day before our God.
And they conquered through the blood of the Lamb and through the word of his testimony, and they did not love their lives even in the face of death.
Therefore rejoice, heavens and those who dwell in them! Woe to the earth and the sea, because the Devil has come down to them in great fury, knowing that he has little time!”
And when the dragon saw that he had been thrown down to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child.
And the woman was given the two wings of a great eagle, so that she could fly into the wilderness to her place, to be fed there for a time, times, and half a time, away from the serpent.
And the serpent poured water like a river out of his mouth after the woman, to have her swept away by the water.
But the earth helped the woman. The earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the dragon had poured out of his mouth.
And the dragon became angry with the woman and went away to wage war against the rest of her offspring, those who keep God's commandments and have the testimony of Jesus.
And I stood on the sand of the sea. And I saw a beast rising out of the sea, with ten horns and seven heads. On its horns were ten crowns, and on its heads was a blasphemous name.
And the beast that I saw resembled a leopard. Its feet were like a bear's, and its mouth was like that of lions. And the dragon gave it his power, his throne, and great authority.
And one of its heads seemed to have been fatally wounded, but its fatal wound was healed. And the whole earth followed the beast in amazement.
And they worshiped the dragon because he had given authority to the beast. And they worshiped the beast, saying, “Who is like this beast, and who can fight against it?”
And it was given a mouth that spoke boasts and blasphemies, and it was given authority to act for forty-two months.
It opened its mouth to blaspheme before God, to blaspheme the name and the dwelling place of those who dwell in heaven.
And it was allowed to wage war against the holy ones and conquer them. And it was given authority over every tribe, nation, language, and people.
And all the inhabitants of the earth will worship it, those who are not written in the book of life belonging to the Lamb who was slain before the foundations of the world.
Whoever has ears, let them hear.
Whoever leads others into captivity goes into captivity. Whoever kills with the sword will be killed with the sword. Here are the faith and endurance of the holy ones.
And I saw another beast rising out of the earth. It had two horns and resembled a lamb, but it spoke like a dragon.
And it will exercise all the authority of the first beast in its presence. It will make the earth and those who live on it worship the first beast, whose fatal wound was healed.
And it will perform great signs, even making fire come down from heaven to earth in front of people.

It deceives those who live on the earth through the signs it was allowed to perform before the beast, telling those who live on the earth to make an image of the beast that had the sword wound and lived.
And it was allowed to give breath to the image of the beast, and it will cause all who do not worship the image of the beast to be killed.
And it will cause everyone, small and great, rich and poor, masters and slaves, to be given a mark on their right hands or on their foreheads,
so that no one can buy or sell anymore except someone who bears the mark of the beast’s name or the number of its name.
Here is wisdom. Let whoever has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a human being: six hundred and sixty-six.
And I saw, and there was the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with him were one hundred and forty-four thousand who had his name and his Father’s name written on their foreheads.
And I heard a sound from heaven like the sound of great waters and like the sound of mighty thunder. The sound I heard was like a harpist playing his harps.

And they sing what sounds like a new song of praise before the throne, before the four living creatures, and before the elders. No one could learn the song except the one hundred and forty-four thousand who had been purchased from the earth.

These are the ones who have not defiled themselves with women, for they are virgins. These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever he goes. These were purchased from among humanity as firstfruits for God and for the Lamb.
No falsehood was found in their mouths, for they are without blemish.
And I saw another angel flying in midheaven, carrying everlasting good news to proclaim to those who live on the earth, to every people, nation, tribe, and language,
saying in a loud voice, “Fear God and give him praise, because the hour of his judgment has come. Worship the one who made heaven and earth and the sea and the springs of water.”
And another, a second, was following him and saying, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, who made all the nations drink from the fury of her sexual immorality.”
And another angel, a third, followed them, saying in a loud voice, “Whoever worships the beast and its image and receives its mark on his forehead,
he too will drink from the wine of the Lord’s fury, prepared undiluted in the cup of his wrath. He will be tormented with fire and sulfur before the holy angels and before the Lamb.
And the smoke of their torment will rise forever and ever. There is no rest day or night for those who worship the beast and its image, or for anyone who receives the mark of its name.”
Here is the endurance of the holy ones, those who keep God’s commandments and faith in Jesus.
And I heard a voice from heaven saying, “Write: Blessed are the dead who die in our Lord from now on.” “Yes,” says the Spirit, “so that they may rest from their labors.”
And look, a white cloud, and seated on the cloud was someone with the likeness of a human being. He had a golden crown on his head and a sharp sickle in his hand.
Another angel came out of the temple and cried out in a loud voice to the one seated on the cloud, “Send out your sickle and reap, because the time to reap has come.”
The one seated on the cloud cast his sickle over the earth, and the earth was reaped.
Another angel came out of the temple in heaven, also carrying a sharp sickle.

Another angel, who had authority over fire, came out from the altar. He cried out in a loud voice to the one who had the sharp sickle, “Send out your sharp sickle and gather the clusters from the earth’s vineyard, because its grapes have ripened.”
The angel swung his sickle over the earth, harvested the earth’s vineyard, and threw it into the great winepress of God’s wrath.
The winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood flowed from the winepress up to the horses’ bridles for a distance of twelve hundred stadia.
I saw another sign in heaven, great and astonishing: angels carrying the seven last plagues, for through them God’s wrath was brought to completion.
I saw what looked like a sea of glass mixed with fire, and those who had overcome the beast, its image, and the number of its name. They were standing above the sea of glass, holding God’s harps.
They sing the song of Moses, God’s servant, and the song of the Lamb, saying, “Great and astonishing are your works, Lord God Almighty. Just and true are your works, King of the ages.
Who will not fear you, Lord, and glorify your name? For you alone are holy. All nations will come and worship before you, because you are upright.”
After these things I looked, and the temple of the tabernacle of testimony in heaven was opened.
The seven angels who carried the seven plagues came out of the temple, dressed in clean, bright linen, with golden sashes fastened around their chests.
One of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven bowls full of the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever. Amen.
The temple was filled with smoke from God’s glory and from his power, and no one could enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.
I heard a loud voice from the temple saying to the seven angels, “Go and pour out the seven bowls of God’s wrath on the earth.”
The first went and poured out his bowl on the earth, and a foul and painful sore broke out on the people who had the mark of the beast and those who worshiped its image.
The second angel poured out his bowl into the sea, and the sea became like a dead person. Every living creature in the sea died.
The third angel poured out his bowl into the rivers and the springs of water, and they became blood.
I heard the angel of the waters saying, “You are righteous, the one who is and who was, and holy, because you have judged these things.
Because they poured out the blood of prophets and holy ones, you have given them blood to drink. They deserve it.”
I heard the altar saying, “Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and righteous are your judgments.”
The fourth angel poured out his bowl on the sun, and it was given power to scorch people with fire.
People were scorched by the intense heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who has authority over these plagues. They did not repent and give him glory.
The fifth angel poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and its kingdom became dark. People were gnawing their tongues because of the pain.
They blasphemed the name of the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and they did not repent of their deeds.
The sixth angel poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its waters dried up so that the way would be prepared for the kings from the east.
I saw three unclean spirits like frogs coming from the mouth of the dragon, from the mouth of the beast, and from the mouth of the false prophet.
For they are spirits of demons that perform signs. They go to the kings of the world to gather them for the battle of that great day of God Almighty.
Look, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who stays awake and guards his clothes, so that he will not walk about naked and people see his shame.
He gathered them to the place called Megiddo in Hebrew.
The seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice came from the temple, from before the throne, saying, “It is done.”
There were flashes of lightning and thunder, and there was a great earthquake. Since people first lived on the earth, there had never been an earthquake like this one, so great was it.
The great city split into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. Babylon the Great was remembered before God, to be given the cup of the wine of his fury and his anger.
Every island fled, and the mountains could not be found.
Huge hailstones, weighing about a talent, fell from heaven on people. People blasphemed God because of the plague of hail, for its plague was exceedingly severe.
One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying, “Come after me. I will show you the judgment of the prostitute who sits on many waters,
with whom the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality, and all the inhabitants of the earth became drunk on the wine of her prostitution.”
He carried me away in the Spirit into the wilderness. I saw a woman sitting on a scarlet beast, which was covered with blasphemous names and had seven heads and ten horns.
The woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, adorned with gold, precious stones, and pearls. She held a golden cup in her hand, full of uncleanness and the filth of her prostitution.
On her forehead was written a mystery: “Babylon the Great, the mother of prostitutes and of the filth of the earth.”
I saw the woman drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the witnesses of Jesus. When I saw her, I was greatly astonished.
The angel said to me, “Why are you astonished? I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has seven heads and ten horns.

The beast that you saw was and is not. It is about to rise from the sea and is going to destruction. The inhabitants of the earth whose names have not been written in the book of life since the foundation of the world will be astonished when they see the beast that was and is not and has drawn near.
Here is understanding for anyone who has wisdom: the seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits.
And they are seven kings. Five have fallen, one exists, and the other has not yet come. When he comes, he is allowed to remain only a short time.
And the dragon and the beast that is and is not: it is the eighth, is one of the seven, and is going to destruction.
The ten horns that you saw are ten kings who have not yet received a kingdom, but they receive authority as kings for one hour with the beast.
These have one purpose, and they give their power and authority to the beast.
These will wage war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will defeat them, because he is Lord of lords and King of kings. Those with him are called, chosen, and faithful.
He said to me, “The waters that you saw, on which the prostitute sits, are peoples, crowds, nations, and languages.”
The ten horns that you saw on the beast will hate the prostitute. They will make her desolate and naked, eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.
For God puts it into their hearts to carry out his purpose, to make their purpose one, and to give their kingdom to that beast until the words of God are fulfilled.
The woman whom you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth.
After these things I saw another angel descending from heaven, having great authority, and the earth was illuminated by his glory.
He cried out with a loud voice, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great! She has become a dwelling place for demons and a prison for all unclean and hateful spirits.”

For she mixed wine from her prostitution for all the nations. The kings of the earth committed sexual immorality with her, and the merchants of the earth became rich through the power of her extravagance.
I heard another voice from heaven saying, “Come out of her, my people, so that you do not share in her sins and receive some of her plagues.”
For sins have clung to her all the way up to heaven, and God has remembered her wrongdoings.
Repay her just as she herself repaid, and pay her back double for her deeds. In the cup in which she mixed her drink, mix a double portion for her.
As much as she glorified and exalted herself, so much torment and mourning. For she says in her heart, “I sit as a queen. I am not a widow, and I will not see mourning.”
Therefore her plagues will come upon her in a single day: death, mourning, and famine. She will be burned with fire, because the Lord who judges her is mighty.
The kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality with her and exalted themselves with her will weep and lament over her when they see the smoke of her burning.
They stand at a distance for fear of her torment and will say, “Woe, woe, woe, great city, Babylon, mighty city! For in one hour your judgment has come.”
The merchants of the earth will weep and mourn over her, and no one buys their cargo anymore.
Cargo of gold, silver, precious stones, pearls, fine linen, purple cloth, scarlet silk, every kind of fragrant wood, every ivory article, and every article of costly wood, bronze, iron, and marble;
and cinnamon, spices, myrrh, frankincense, wine, oil, fine flour, sheep, horses, chariots, and human bodies and souls.
The fruit your soul desired has gone from you. Everything rich and splendid has gone from you, and you will never see them again.
And the merchants of these things, who grew rich from her, will not find them. They will stand at a distance for fear of her torment, weeping and mourning
and saying, “Alas, alas, the great city, clothed in fine linen, purple, and scarlet garments adorned with gold, precious stones, and pearls!
For in a single hour such wealth has been emptied away!” And all shipmasters, all who travel by ship to various places, sailors, and all who work at sea stood at a distance.
They wept when they saw the smoke of her burning and said, “What city is like the great city?”

They threw dust on their heads and cried out, weeping and mourning and saying, “Alas, alas, the great city, in which those who have ships at sea grew rich from her wealth! For in a single hour she has been laid waste!”
Rejoice over her, heaven, and you saints, apostles, and prophets, because God has judged her on your behalf.
One of the mighty angels picked up a large stone like a millstone, threw it into the sea, and said, “With such violence Babylon, the great city, will be thrown down and will never be found again.
The sound of the harp, the trumpet, various kinds of music, and pipes will never be heard in you again.

The light of a lamp will never be seen in you again, and the voice of a bridegroom and the voice of a bride will never be heard in you again, because your merchants were the great ones of the earth, and because you deceived all the nations by your sorceries.”
And in her was found the blood of prophets and saints who had been killed on the earth.
After these things I heard the loud voice of great crowds in heaven saying, “Hallelujah! Salvation, glory, and power belong to our God,
because his judgments are true and just. For he has judged the great prostitute who corrupted the earth with her prostitution, and he has avenged the blood of his servants at her hands.”
A second time they said, “Hallelujah!” And her smoke rises forever and ever.
The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped our God, who sits on the throne, saying, “Amen! Hallelujah!”
And a voice from the throne said, “Praise our God, all his servants and those who fear his name, all of you, small and great.”
I heard a sound like that of great crowds, like the sound of many waters, and like the sound of mighty thunder, saying, “Hallelujah! For the Lord God Almighty reigns.
We rejoice and are glad. Let us give him glory, because the wedding feast of the Lamb has come, and his wife has made herself ready.
She was granted fine linen, pure and bright, to wear.” For the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints.
They said to me, “Write: Blessed are those who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb.” And he said to me, “These are the true words of God.”

I fell down before his feet and worshiped him. He said to me, “No! I am a fellow servant of yours and of your brothers who have the testimony of Jesus. Worship God instead! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”
I saw heaven opened, and there was a white horse! Its rider is called Faithful and True, and he judges and wages war in righteousness.
His eyes were like a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns. He had a name written that no one knows except himself.
He is clothed in a garment spattered with blood, and his name is called the Word of God.
And the armies of heaven were following him on white horses, dressed in fine linen, white and clean.
And from their mouths comes a sharp sword, with which they will kill the nations. And he will shepherd them with an iron rod, and he treads the winepress of the wrath of God Almighty.
And on his clothing, on his thighs, he has a name written: King of kings and Lord of lords.
I saw another angel standing in the sun. He cried out in a loud voice and said to the birds flying in midair, “Come, gather for the great supper of God.”

So that you may eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of commanders of thousands, the flesh of mighty men, the flesh of horses and those who ride them, and the flesh of free people and slaves, small and great.
And I saw the beast and its armies, and the kings of the earth and their soldiers, gathered to wage war against the one sitting on the horse and against his soldiers.

And the beast was captured, and with it the false prophet who had performed signs in its presence, by which he deceived those who had received the beast’s mark and those who had worshiped its image. Both of them went down and were thrown into the lake of burning fire and sulfur.
And the rest were killed by the sword of the one sitting on the horse, the sword that comes from his mouth. And all the birds ate their fill of their flesh.
And I saw another angel coming down from heaven, carrying the key to the abyss, with a great chain in his hand.
And he seized the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years.
And he threw him into the abyss, shut it, and sealed it over him so that he would no longer deceive all the nations. After these things, he is to be released for a short time.

I saw thrones, and people sat on them, and authority to judge was given to them. I also saw the souls of those who had been beheaded because of their testimony to Jesus and because of the word of God, and of those who had not worshiped the beast or its image and had not received the mark on their foreheads or on their hands. They came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.
And this is the first resurrection.

Blessed and holy is anyone who has a share in the first resurrection. The second death has no power over these people, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and they will reign with him for a thousand years.
And when the thousand years are completed, Satan will be released from his prison.
And he will go out to deceive all the nations at the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, and to gather them for battle. Their number is like the sand of the sea.
And they advanced across the breadth of the earth and surrounded the city of the camp of the holy ones and the beloved city. And fire came down from heaven, from God, and consumed them.
And the devil who deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet are. And they will be tormented day and night forever and ever.
And I saw a great white throne and the one sitting on it. Earth and heaven fled from his presence, and no place was found for them.

And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne. And books were opened, and another book was opened, which is the book of judgment. And the dead were judged according to their deeds, from what was written in the book.
And the sea gave up the dead who were in it, and Death and Sheol gave up the dead who were with them. And each one of them was judged according to their deeds.
Death and Sheol were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death.
And anyone who was not found recorded in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.
And I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more.
And I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.
And I heard a loud voice from heaven saying, “Look! God’s dwelling is with human beings. He will dwell with them, and they will be his people. God himself will be with them and will be their God.
He will wipe every tear from their eyes, and there will be no more death, nor mourning, nor outcry, nor will there be pain upon it anymore.”
And I went, and the one seated on the throne said to me, “Look! I am making everything new.” And he said to me, “Write, for these words are trustworthy and true.”
And he said to me, “They have come to pass. I am Aleph, and I am Taw, the beginning and the end. To anyone who is thirsty I will freely give water from the spring of living water.
Whoever overcomes will inherit these things, and I will be his God, and he will be my son.

But as for the cowardly, the unbelieving, the wicked, the defiled, murderers, sorcerers, the sexually immoral, idol worshipers, and all liars, their share is in the lake burning with fire and sulfur, which is the second death.”
And one of the seven angels who held the seven bowls filled with the seven last plagues came and spoke with me, saying, “Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb.”
And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great, high mountain and showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God.
It had the glory of God, and its radiance was like a precious stone, like jasper, resembling crystal.
It had a great, high wall and twelve gates, with twelve angels at the gates. Their names were written there—the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.
On the east were three gates, on the north three gates, on the south three gates, and on the west three gates.
The wall of the city has twelve foundations, and on them are the twelve names of the apostles of the Son.
The one who was speaking with me held a golden measuring rod to measure the city and its wall.
The city was laid out as a square, its length equal to its width. He measured the city with the rod: twelve thousand stadia. Its length, width, and height were equal.
And he measured its wall: one hundred and forty-four cubits, by human measurement, which was also the angel’s measurement.
The structure of its wall was jasper, and the city was pure gold, like clear glass.
The foundations of the city wall were adorned with precious stones. The first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, and the fourth emerald.
The fifth was sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst.
And the twelve gates were twelve pearls, one for each gate. Each of the gates was made from a single pearl. And the city's street was pure gold, like glass.
And I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God Almighty is its temple.
For the Lamb and the city, neither the sun nor the moon is needed to shine on it, for the glory of God has illuminated it, and its lamp is the Lamb.
And the nations walk by its light, and the kings of the earth bring glory to it.
And its gates will not be shut during the day, for there will be no night there.
And they will bring into it the glory and honor of the nations.
And nothing unclean will be there, nor anyone who practices defilement and falsehood, but only those who are written in the Lamb's book.
And he showed me a river of living water, pure and bright as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb.
And in the middle of its streets, on either side of the river, was the tree of life, producing twelve crops of fruit and yielding its fruit every month. Its leaves are for the healing of the nations.
And there will be no curse there. The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will serve him.
And they will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads.
And there will be no night there. They will have no need of light, or of a lamp or the light of the sun, because the Lord God gives them light. And their reign will last forever and ever.
And he said to me, "These words are trustworthy and true. And the Lord, the God of the spirits of the holy prophets, sent his angel to show his servants what is appointed to happen soon."
"And look, I am coming soon. Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book."
I am John, who saw and heard these things. And when I saw and heard them, I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who was showing me these things.
And he said to me, "See that you do not do that! I am a fellow servant of yours, of your brothers the prophets, and of those who keep these words of this book. Worship God."
And he said to me, "Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near.
Let the one who does wrong continue to do wrong, and let the filthy one continue to be filthy. Let the righteous one continue to do what is right, and let the holy one continue to be made holy."
"Look, I am coming soon, and my reward is with me. I will give to everyone according to their deeds.
I am Aleph and I am Taw, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
Blessed are those who obey his commandments, so that they may have the right to the tree of life and may enter the city through the gate.
Outside are the sexually immoral, murderers, and idol worshipers, the unclean and sorcerers, and all who see and practice falsehood.
I, Jesus, sent my angel to testify to you about these things before the churches. I am the root and offspring of David and his people, and the bright morning star."
And the Spirit and the bride say, "Come." And let whoever hears say, "Come." And let whoever is thirsty come and take living water freely.
I testify to everyone who hears the message of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to these things, God will add to that person the plagues written in this book.
And if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away that person's share in the tree of life and in the holy city, which are written about in this book.
He who testifies to these things says, “Yes, I am coming soon.” Come, Lord Jesus!
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all his holy ones. Amen.
